speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me your age and describe how these skin lesions first appeared? I also need to know if they are itchy, painful, or if you have had any recent fevers or illnesses.

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the papules umbilicated (dimpled in the center) or dome-shaped, and do they have a pearly or waxy appearance? Have you noticed any spreading of the lesions to other parts of the body, or any signs of secondary bacterial infection like redness or pus?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of pearly, umbilicated papules is classic for Molluscum Contagiosum, especially given the daycare exposure. I am confident in this clinical diagnosis and do not require further testing. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
